summary: Implemented automatic exit after successful final-summary delivery for completed and skipped simplification. Preserved workflow files, unrelated tools, and foreign prompt sections. Updated coordinator guidance and user documentation.

acceptanceCriteria.probe: Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts -t 'when the final response finishes|when a later response finishes'. The completed-simplification scenario uses the real registered tool and saved S.json with summary 'No simplification needed'; Maestro becomes inactive after the scripted final response completes without /maestro.

Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts -t 'when the final response finishes|when a later response finishes'. The skipped-simplification scenario returns false from Git readiness, saves candidate-ready through the real tool, delivers the skip summary, and observes Maestro inactive afterward.

Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts -t 'when the final response finishes|when a later response finishes'. Real Pi tool-execution and text-delta events show Maestro still active after the terminal tool result and during final-summary streaming, including the 'Simplified counting' report. It exits only when the response finishes successfully.

Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts -t 'when the final response finishes|when a later response finishes'. Failed, cancelled via session.abort(), and truncated final responses all leave Maestro active after candidate-ready is saved. Additional scenarios confirm saved completion alone, a failed terminal tool result, another spec's completion, and a later prompt without completed delivery do not trigger exit.

Ran ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts -t 'when the final response finishes|when a later response finishes'. Successful scenarios start with read, foreign_tool, and Maestro tools; afterward the active spec is null, only read and foreign_tool remain active, status is unset, and the next prompt preserves foreign instructions without Maestro's section. A real queued-follow-up request also observes restored mode, tools, and prompt sections. Saved workflow, spec, verifier report, and available simplifier report remain byte-identical.

notes: npm run check passed: formatting, lint, typecheck, and all 262 tests across 40 files, including coverage thresholds. The final focused acceptance/regression run passed all 11 selected scenarios. git diff --check passed.

Pi processes queued follow-ups before agent_end. Automatic exit therefore uses the successful assistant message_end boundary, with agent_end clearing unfinished pending delivery. Inactive request-context filtering removes only Maestro's named prompt section without editing saved history.
Linear MCP tools were unavailable, so MAESTRO-26 could not be read or updated. Existing approved documents identify and link the issue. No owner acceptance or roadmap completion is claimed.
No dependencies or structural files were added. Test fixtures use existing temporary-project cleanup; no temporary verification files were added to the project.
